title: CHU de la Guadeloupe hospital cyberattack, Nov 21, 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by CHU de la Guadeloupe, ANSSI, any news outlet, government agency, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: The hospital says all three of its sites are affected with varying impact, and it has cancelled non-urgent care through Nov 27. It has not given patient numbers.
who_is_affected: Patients and staff of the CHU de la Guadeloupe, in Guadeloupe, France. Urgent care continues; scheduled surgery, consultations and imaging are being cancelled through Nov 27, and patients are told to call the emergency dispatch line before coming.

known.text: The hospital's director says a cyberattack began Saturday evening, Nov 21, and blocked its IT systems and phones.
Some of the hospital's databases were encrypted and are not accessible.
The hospital is on paper procedures, with phones, imaging, lab and software disrupted.
The plan blanc is on and non-urgent care is cancelled through Nov 27.
The national cybersecurity agency is helping and has told the hospital to expect a long recovery.
The Paris prosecutor's cybercrime section opened an investigation on Nov 23.

not_known.text: Whether the attackers really came in through a hacked IT supplier, and which one.
Whether patient data was stolen, and whether a ransom will be demanded; none had been by Nov 23.
When systems will be fully back; the director says there is no visibility before the end of the week, when a full diagnosis is expected.
